title: Closed containment locus for a Hilbert subscheme
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $T$ be a scheme over $S$ and write $X_T=X\times_S T$ [def-pc-base-change]. Let $i:W\hookrightarrow X_T$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $Z\hookrightarrow X_T$ be a closed subscheme whose structure morphism $Z\to T$ is finite locally free of degree $d$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Then there exists a closed subscheme $T_W\hookrightarrow T$ such that, for every morphism $T'\to T$ over $S$, the pullback $Z_{T'}\hookrightarrow X_{T'}$ factors through $W_{T'}\hookrightarrow X_{T'}$ if and only if $T'\to T$ factors through $T_W\hookrightarrow T$. The construction is compatible with arbitrary base change in $T$.

source.place: Picard Schemes of Curves, Lemma 44.2.7, label lemma-hilb-d-of-closed, Tag 0B97

proof.text: The assertion is local on the base $T$. For an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ of $T$, the inverse image $Z_U$ of $U$ in $Z$ is affine, say $Z_U=\operatorname{Spec}(B)$, because $Z\to T$ is finite; as $Z\to T$ is finite locally free, $B$ is a finitely presented flat, hence finite projective, $R$-module. The inverse image of $W$ in $Z_U$ is a closed subscheme $\operatorname{Spec}(B/J_U)$ for an ideal $J_U\subseteq B$. The affine coefficient lemma [lem-pc-affine-containment-ideal] gives an ideal $K_U\subseteq R$ such that, for every ring map $R\to R'$, the image of $J_U$ in $B\otimes_R R'$ is zero if and only if the image of $K_U$ in $R'$ is zero.

source.place: Picard Schemes of Curves, Lemma 44.2.7, label lemma-hilb-d-of-closed, Tag 0B97

proof.text: For $f\in R$ and the principal open $U_f=\operatorname{Spec}(R_f)$ we have $Z_{U_f}=\operatorname{Spec}(B_f)$ and $J_{U_f}=J_UB_f$, so both $K_{U_f}$ and the extension $K_UR_f$ satisfy the vanishing property of Step 1 for every ring map $R_f\to R'$. Testing on the quotient maps $R_f\to R_f/I$ shows that each of them is contained in every ideal $I$ containing the other, so $K_{U_f}=K_UR_f$ (elementary). Thus the family $(K_U)_U$ over all affine opens $U$ of $T$ satisfies the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme] and defines a closed immersion $T_W\to T$ whose ideal sheaf has sections $K_U$ on every affine open $U$.

source.place: Picard Schemes of Curves, Lemma 44.2.7, label lemma-hilb-d-of-closed, Tag 0B97

proof.text: Let $T'\to T$ be a morphism over $S$ and cover $T'$ by affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}(R')$ each mapping into an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ of $T$; then $Z_{T'}$ is covered by the affines $Z_V=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_R R')$, and the ideal of $W_{T'}$ restricted to $Z_V$ is generated by the image of $J_U$. Suppose $T'\to T$ factors through $T_W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-factor-ideal-inclusion] the ideal sheaf of $T_W$ pulls back to zero on $T'$, so $K_U$ maps to zero in $R'$ for every such $V$, hence by [lem-pc-affine-containment-ideal] the image of $J_U$ in $B\otimes_R R'$ is zero; so the ideal sheaf of $W_{T'}$ maps to zero in $\mathcal O_{Z_{T'}}$ on every member of an affine cover, hence on every affine open of $X_{T'}$ by the sheaf property, and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-lift-ideal-kills-sections] gives a factorization $Z_{T'}\to W_{T'}$. Conversely, if $Z_{T'}\to X_{T'}$ factors through $W_{T'}$, then by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-factor-ideal-inclusion] the ideal sheaf of $W_{T'}$ is contained in that of $Z_{T'}$, so the image of $J_U$ in $B\otimes_R R'$ is zero for every $V$, hence $K_U$ maps to zero in $R'$ by [lem-pc-affine-containment-ideal]; thus the ideal sheaf of $T_W$ maps to zero in $\mathcal O_{T'}$ on an affine cover of $T'$, hence on every affine open of $T$, and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-lift-ideal-kills-sections] gives a factorization of $T'\to T$ through $T_W$. This proves the equivalence. Compatibility with base change: for $T''\to T$, the closed subscheme $T_W\times_T T''$ satisfies the same universal property for $Z_{T''}$ and $W_{T''}$ (a morphism to $T''$ factors through it if and only if its composite to $T$ factors through $T_W$), so by the equivalence just proved and the Yoneda argument it coincides with $(T'')_{W_{T''}}$ (elementary).

lean.statement:
theorem exists_idealSheafData_le_ker_iff_comap_le {d : ℕ} {T : Over S}
    {I : (pullback f T.hom).IdealSheafData} (hI : IsHilbertSubscheme f d T I)
    (J : (pullback f T.hom).IdealSheafData) :
    ∃ K : T.left.IdealSheafData, ∀ (T' : Over S) (φ : T' ⟶ T),
      K ≤ φ.left.ker ↔ J.comap (baseChangeMap f φ) ≤ I.comap (baseChangeMap f φ)
lean.note: Second reading: the source theorem already has exactly this universal containment property, with arbitrary X, S and f from section Relative. Closed subschemes are equivalently IdealSheafData; compatibility with arbitrary base change follows from its universal property and uniqueness. Its proof is sorry; stage 2 records existing statements regardless of proof status.
